overview: The Urban Innovation Challenge (UIC) – MoHUA is a scheme under the Urban Challenge Fund (UCF) that aims to catalyse a paradigm shift in urban development by encouraging cities to transition towards market-based financing and integrated regional development. It positions cities as a bankable asset class through targeted reforms, strengthened institutional capacity, improved governance and planning frameworks, and the development of sustainable revenue-generating urban infrastructure. The scheme supports urban transformation through three verticals: 'Cities as Growth Hubs', 'Creative Redevelopment of Cities', and 'Water and Sanitation'.
objectives: Catalyse a paradigm shift in urban development by encouraging cities to transition towards market-based financing and integrated regional development
Position cities as a bankable asset class through targeted reforms and strengthened institutional capacity
Improve governance and planning frameworks for sustainable revenue-generating urban infrastructure
Support urban transformation through three verticals: 'Cities as Growth Hubs', 'Creative Redevelopment of Cities', and 'Water and Sanitation'
Leverage significantly larger investments from market-based sources using Central Assistance as a catalytic instrument
Ensure projects remain financially viable and sustainable across their entire life cycle
Focus on strengthening Tier II and Tier III cities with specific coverage criteria
eligibility: All States and UTs are eligible to participate in UCF with a specific focus on strengthening Tier II and Tier III cities. The following categories of cities shall be covered under UCF: All cities with a projected 2025 population of 10 lakh or more; Capital cities of State/UT not included in the first category; Major industrial cities (Manufacturing & Services) with a projected 2025 population of 1,00,000 or more; All Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) in Hilly States/UTs, Northeastern States; and ULBs with population below 1,00,000 in other States/UTs. As per above, all ULBs are eligible to participate in UCF.
benefits: Central Assistance (CA) acts as catalytic support to leverage market-based financing, enable structured project implementation, and ensure timely execution of financially viable and reform-linked urban infrastructure investments. The fund supports projects across three verticals: Digital Governance, Development of Trunk Infrastructure, Circularity, Projects for decongestion, Last mile connectivity infrastructure, Revitalisation of old city areas, Redevelopment of old markets, Non-motorised transport infrastructure, Transit Hub upgradation, TOD infrastructure development, Projects for prevention of urban flooding, Integrated waste processing, Green field/ Semi Greenfield City infrastructure, Development of road infrastructure and flyovers, Riverfront development, and Projects required for implementation of reforms.
financial_support: The Urban Challenge Fund provides a total Central Assistance (CA) of ₹1,00,000 crore over the Mission period. The Central Assistance (CA) is designed as a catalytic instrument to leverage significantly larger investments from market-based sources. The CA for projects is limited to 25 percent of the cost of bankable projects with a stipulation that at least 50 percent of the project cost is funded from bonds, bank loans, and PPPs. The Central Assistance for UCF is structured as: Projects: ₹90,000 crore; Project Preparation and Capacity Building at National, State/UT, and City levels: ₹5,000 crore; and Credit Repayment Guarantee Sub-Scheme (CRGSS): ₹5,000 crore.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)
